clue.text: Doctor seen in unusual haste at the sauna

indicators.note: the doctor is seen inside the rearranged letters, so these words place one piece within another
unusual signals that the letters of haste at are put in an unusual order

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone notices their physician hurrying oddly through the spa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges HASTE AT into STEAATH, and 'seen in' puts MB inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Turkish-style hot room filled with vapour is what a sauna is, so both name the same steamy bathing room.

indicators.note: initial asks for only the opening letter of the word The

parts.note: a mistake is an error

explanation.surface: The first blunder is what sets off widespread alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial' looks like an adjective for the mistake, but it takes the first letter of 'The'.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic and its stronger synonym both describe overwhelming fear.

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A remark about removing doubts once you are confident.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from doubt is to reassure or convince them, a verb synonym.

indicators.note: in places the word He inside the word for highest

parts.note: best means highest in quality
taken as written

explanation.surface: He sits at the top of the chain of command.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is an order or instruction given by someone in authority.

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of hear out could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An invitation to listen to an American author.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Walden was an American essayist and naturalist.

clue.text: They get fed up with people

definitions.text: They get fed up with people

parts.words: They get fed up with people
parts.note: read as being sick of humans, but literally it describes those who dine on humans

explanation.definitionFit: Man-eaters are literally fed full of humans, which is the joke behind 'fed up with people'.

clue.text: Striker on trial in international game

indicators.note: on joins the two pieces, the striker attached next to the trial

parts.note: a test is a trial
a match is struck to light it, so it is a striker

explanation.surface: A footballer on trial in a game between countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer, but it is the thing you strike to make fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A test match is a game between national sides, especially in cricket or rugby.

indicators.note: rough signals the letters of Treading are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: Walking over rough ground on the southern hillsides.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradients are inclines, the degree to which a road or hill rises.

clue.text: Make rapid progress in a profession

definitions.meaning: to rush along at speed, hurtling forward
one's working life or chosen occupation

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for rushing headlong and a noun for one's lifelong occupation.

clue.text: Customised Porsche, original wings, about three years old

indicators.note: customised means altered to taste, so the letters are refashioned
the wings of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A modified sports car with its original wings, dating back about three years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings' gives O and L, the first and last letters of 'original'; 'Customised' mixes them with PORSCHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery-age children, around three, attend schooling before formal school starts.

definitions.meaning: a name shared by many football teams, such as Manchester's or Leeds's

explanation.definitionFit: The word means joined together, and is also part of many British football club names, like Manchester United.

clue.text: He is round, although poorly fed

indicators.note: poorly signals the letters of He is round are badly arranged

explanation.surface: He is plump, even though he eats badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' looks like it describes the feeding, but it rearranges HE IS ROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: To be nourished is to have been given food, so fed is a synonym.

clue.text: Burning a mark on a horse

parts.note: a blaze is a white stripe down a horse's face

explanation.surface: Branding a horse with a hot iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on fire is aflame, so burning is a synonym.

parts.note: booked means put together in a book title, alongside the word pride, as in Jane Austen's novel

explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's novel title pairs this bias with pride, so it is literally booked with pride.

definitions.meaning: a British weekly political and cultural magazine founded in 1828

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an onlooker, and is also the name of a long-running British weekly periodical.

clue.text: The followers stand here when assembled

indicators.note: assembled means put together, so the letters of stand here are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: The fans are told to line up here when gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherents are supporters who stick to a cause or leader, so followers is a synonym.

indicators.note: no signals that the word for nonsense is removed from Robust

parts.note: rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: A sturdy, practical car or van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no-nonsense' reads as one adjective, but it says remove ROT from ROBUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A public transport coach on roads is a type of vehicle.

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a run scored without the ball touching the bat
in a knockout competition, a free pass to the next round without playing

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket it is a run added to the total, and in a cup it is a free passage to the next round.

parts.note: reads as an unpopular teacher, but miss is what pupils call a female teacher, and they would not call a male teacher that

explanation.definitionFit: British pupils address a male teacher this way, and a female teacher as miss.

clue.text: Quickly knock but to no avail

parts.note: a rap is a knock
idly can mean pointlessly, to no avail

explanation.surface: Someone bangs on a door quickly but nobody answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidly and quickly are both adverbs of speed.

clue.text: It's forbidden, and badly one hundred take it

parts.note: ill means badly, as in ill-treated
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something banned, and a hundred people put up with it poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit things are not allowed by law or rule, so they are banned.

definitions.meaning: the seed-bearing head of a cereal plant such as maize
the body part used for hearing

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a head of corn and also the hearing organ.

clue.text: Runner allowed to take part in a different heat

indicators.note: taking part in something means being inside it, so one piece goes within another
different signals the letters of heat are made different

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: A sprinter is permitted to compete in another qualifying race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' turns HEAT into ATHE, and 'to take part in' puts LET inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter or distance competitor is a sportsperson who runs.
As a verb it means to jostle for advantage; as a noun it is a professional race rider.

clue.text: It's divine if iced ingredients are used

indicators.note: the letters of if iced are used as ingredients and mixed into something new

explanation.surface: A cake becomes heavenly when frosting is part of the recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deific is godlike or making divine, from Latin deus, god.

parts.note: Stan, not Oliver Hardy of the comedy double act, but also a glossy-leaved shrub that keeps its leaves

explanation.definitionFit: Stan of the comedy duo was the partner of Hardy, and the bay tree is an evergreen shrub.

clue.text: Dismissive order to a drummer perhaps

definitions.text: Dismissive order to a drummer perhaps

parts.words: Dismissive order to a drummer perhaps
parts.note: a rude way of telling someone to go away, which a drummer could take literally as play the drum

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for go away, and a drummer would literally strike the drum.

clue.text: He has found a job at last

definitions.text: He has found a job at last

parts.words: He has found a job at last
parts.note: reads as someone ending unemployment, but a last is the foot-shaped mould a cobbler works on

explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler shapes footwear on a last, so his work is literally done at the last.

indicators.note: back signals the word for pay is read backwards

parts.note: a reward is a payment

explanation.surface: An artist receives his arrears of salary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back pay' looks like arrears, but 'back' turns REWARD around.
explanation.definitionFit: One who draws pictures or plans is a draughtsman.

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters of of Trieste are disturbed

explanation.surface: The lights of an Italian port city have been switched off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' suggests extinguishing, the opposite of the answer, but it rearranges OF TRIESTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a fire is to ignite it, a verb synonym.

definitions.meaning: heavy blows, as in ... round the ear
an old word for rags or garments

explanation.definitionFit: The word means hard blows and is also an old dialect word for garments, as in 'cast ne'er a clout'.

clue.text: Filter supplied by firm with some delay

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A water filter supplied by a company arrives late.
explanation.definitionFit: To percolate is to seep or pass through a filter.
